newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH INDUSTRY CRITICAL OF M&A MONITOR PLAN.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH INDUSTRY CRITICAL OF M&A MONITOR PLAN.

text.p: The Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers TT said on Thursday a ministry working group proposal to start monitoring corporate mergers and acquisitions would cause more problems that it would solve.

"The problems would be especially big for small- and medium-sized enterprises that are the target of acquisition," TT said in a statement referring to the proposal by a trade and industry ministry working group.

Under the proposal, the competition authority could forbid a deal which would result in the creation of strengthening of a dominant market position and significantly impede competition, the ministry said earlier in a statement.
The proposal would affect deals in which all parties had combined net sales of over two billion markka and in which at least two parties had net sales over 200 million markka.
"The working group's proposed limits for monitoring of corporate acquisitions are quite low in comparison with the situation in other countries," TT said.

It added that in Germany and France, monitoring only affected deals concerning parties with net sales over six billion markka, and that the corresponding limit in Sweden was almost three billion markka.

The proposal will be circulated widely for comment this spring and the government plans to put a bill before parliament before the end of the year, Minister of Trade and Industry Antti Kalliomaki told a news conference.
